root_cause_verified.observed_failure: stage-runtime02 legacy load_and_validate constructs a standard policy ModuleSpec while its util.module_from_spec resolves to the active bridge10 graph-only facade; bridge10 rejects the foreign spec before frozen policy authority checks.
root_cause_verified.latent_ordinary_route: The ordinary pinned graph route has the same split-factory risk: a standard ModuleSpec can reach a graph-only module_from_spec. Repairing only the observed policy branch would move the failure to a late executor, checker, or resource loader.
actual_call_path: bridge10._module_from_spec rejecting a foreign graph import spec

paired_factories.legacy_policy_compatibility: covered by a StageImportFactoryPair compatibility route bound to the exact historical policy path, SHA, selector, and pinned policy object; no source re-execution
paired_factories.ordinary_graph_spec: covered by an explicit graph-pinned route with exact member/path/SHA/loader binding; the implementation must exercise it through the actual frozen route, not a generated projection
paired_factories.graph_facade_separation: the graph-owned _GraphSpec facade and stage-owned factory pair remain distinct and reject each other's specs

strong_registry: strong spec reference and identity check
per-stage factory nonce and graph context identity
explicit route kind, selector/name, canonical path and source SHA
exact target module object and exact loader object
rejection of copied/reconstructed specs, foreign scopes, wrong routes, changed bytes, and changed targets
design_checks.identity_and_lifetime: One immutable pair is reused by the stage and every nested legacy/provider/checker/resource owner in one stage scope; nested scopes detect and reuse the marked pair rather than wrapping it with a second registry. A later stage may have a fresh graph, but no serialized runtime object is treated as authority.
design_checks.metadata_and_restoration: The design snapshots target metadata, owner importlib attributes, stage globals, and local synthetic registrations, then restores exact prior values in reverse order on success and exception.
design_checks.stdlib_capture: The real stdlib spec_from_file_location, module_from_spec, and ModuleSpec constructor are captured before any graph facade installation and passed explicitly; the implementation cannot rediscover them through an already-patched stage global.
design_checks.global_patch_rejection: No global sys.path, process-global importlib, or unbound sys.modules alias is permitted; foreign specs, duplicate routes, ambiguous first matches, and second source execution fail closed.
design_checks.full_validator_preserved: The copied load_and_validate/load_runtime_context body and all source, contract, qualification, executor, checker, configuration, historical, resource, and context checks remain in the successor; only scoped factory and exact route bindings change.

required_implementation_evidence.actual_frozen_policy_path: Drive the real successor create_parent_stage through the actual load_and_validate policy import at stage-runtime02 line 1172 and show that the exact pinned policy object reaches the frozen validator.
required_implementation_evidence.actual_frozen_pinned_path: Drive one real ordinary graph-pinned route and one late executor/checker/resource loader through the same stage pair; show exact target identity and zero source re-execution.
required_implementation_evidence.actual_composed_scopes: Exercise full graph scope plus provider/nested scope, proving pair reuse, exact route selection, policy compatibility, ordinary graph-spec handling, and complete restoration after success.
near_miss_rejections: StageImportFactory standard spec passed to GraphImportlibFacade.module_from_spec
copied/reconstructed standard spec with equal visible fields but no registry identity
wrong historical policy path/SHA or successor policy under the historical selector
ambiguous, reordered, wrong-name, wrong-path, changed-SHA, or foreign graph member
second pair nonce or nested wrapper around the same graph
loader/source re-execution or leaked metadata/importlib/module state after an exception
required_implementation_evidence.route_coverage: All 88 graph members, the known bare/dynamic routes, eager SCC ordering, and all known late executor/checker/resource imports must be bound and tested; key/count-only or synthetic-frame tests are insufficient.
required_implementation_evidence.fresh_successor_binding: Successor bridge/stage/runtime-loader sources, tests, source closure, plan, contract, manifest, and qualification hashes must be produced append-only and independently reviewed. Future hashes are intentionally unknown in this design artifact.

preserved_boundaries: BF15 source, plan, contract, manifest, core, graph, ledger prefix, stop records, and reviews remain immutable predecessor evidence.
The 89-row ledger and zero-attempt state at the stopped boundary remain unchanged.
Original clock, no-expiry authority, resource/reserve/scratch/retention/per-attempt/one-slot/analyzer guards, and automatic_retry false remain bound.
Configuration remains deferred and outside this implementation-only decision.
conditional_followups: This approval authorizes implementation preparation only; it does not authorize source commit, build, graph/runtime qualification, replay, admission, analyzer dispatch, retry, or launch.
The successor implementation must receive a fresh independent source/graph review with actual-function-path tests before any new qualification invocation.
A later candidate must preserve the exact BF15 stop evidence and bind any new source/plan/contract/manifest identities without relabeling historical files.
